findings.description: `srcSources`/`testSources` are built by walking only `readdirSync(packagesDir)` (`packages/*`). `pnpm-workspace.yaml` also lists `features` (and `examples/*`, `apps/*`) as workspace members outside `packages/`. `features/step-definitions/*.ts` alone has 43 non-test `.ts` files (BDD step implementations) that are never scanned, so none of AGENTS.md's Effect-specific rules — no async/await, no type assertions, no raw Promise, Context.Service/Data.TaggedError enforcement, no node:fs — are ever checked there. `.oxlintrc.json`'s `ignorePatterns` (only `features/lib/**`) confirms the toolchain otherwise treats `features/` as in-scope for linting, so this is a real gap rather than a deliberate exclusion. This is the same shape of blind spot CCR-QD-105 already found and fixed for `packages/*/test` (a scope that silently hid violations), just one directory root over.
findings.suggestedFix: Also collect `features/step-definitions` (and decide deliberately about `examples/*`/`apps/*`) into `srcSources`/`testSources`, or document the exclusion explicitly the way EXEMPTIONS documents per-file exceptions.

findings.description: `no-node-fs-import`'s regex is `/from\s+["']node:fs["']/`, which matches only the exact specifier `"node:fs"`. `import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises"` or `import fs from "fs"` (the un-prefixed legacy specifier) reach the identical banned Node filesystem API and are not caught — the gate can be defeated by a one-word change to the import specifier while violating exactly the AGENTS.md §6 rule it exists to enforce ("use the FileSystem service, not node:fs directly").
findings.suggestedFix: Broaden the pattern to something like /from\s+["'](?:node:)?fs(?:\/promises)?["']/ so the promises subpath and the unprefixed specifier are both caught.

findings.description: `readdirSync(FOLDER).filter((entry) => entry.endsWith(".md"))` only looks at the top level of `spec/devtools-spec/` — it does not recurse into subdirectories the way the sibling collectors do (`check-dod-table.mjs`'s and `check-doc-examples.mjs`'s `collectMarkdown` both recurse). Today `spec/devtools-spec/` happens to have no subdirectories (verified: `find spec/devtools-spec -type d` returns only the folder itself), so this passes now, but a claim of absence written into a future subdirectory of that folder would never be scanned by this gate — a silent gap in exactly the "no silent omission" guarantee this script exists to provide (its own doc comment cites CCR-QD-074's seven false claims as the reason it exists).
findings.suggestedFix: Recurse into subdirectories the same way check-dod-table.mjs's collectMarkdown does, or add a comment explaining why the folder is guaranteed to stay flat.

findings.description: Only a missing `start` anchor raises a `[missing-anchor]` failure (`if (from === -1) fail(...)`). There is no equivalent check on `to` — if `content.indexOf(end, from) === -1`, the code silently falls back to `section = content.slice(from)`, scanning from the anchor to the end of the file. If any of the four `end` markers (e.g. README.md's `"\n\n## Why"`) is ever renamed or reworded, the gate will not report the drift the way it does for a missing `start`; instead it silently widens the scanned window to the rest of the document, which can pick up unrelated version literals or "unpublished"-type phrasing from later sections (e.g. a changelog excerpt) as spurious matches, or fail to notice that the real publish-status paragraph moved past where `TARGETS` expects it.
findings.suggestedFix: Fail loudly when `to === -1` too (mirroring the `from === -1` check), the same way check-dod-table.mjs and check-devtools-claims.mjs treat 'checker found nothing to check' as a hard error rather than a silent widen.

findings.description: `parseLeg` does `leg.split(".").map(Number)` then `parts[1] ?? 0` for the minor version. `??` only substitutes on `null`/`undefined`, not `NaN`, so a non-numeric segment (e.g. a matrix leg written as `"20.x"`, a common CI shorthand) produces `minor: NaN` rather than falling back to `0`. Verified directly: `satisfiesFloor(parseLeg("20.x"))` against the current `>=20.19.0` floor returns `false` (major ties at 20, then `NaN - 19` is `NaN`, and `NaN >= 0` is `false`), even though "20.x" in practice resolves to a patch of Node 20 well above 20.19.0. The current workflow matrix (`["20.19.0", "26"]`) doesn't hit this, but if a maintainer ever writes a matrix leg with a non-numeric segment, the script would silently misjudge that leg as not satisfying the floor, and — if it were the matrix's only leg — would incorrectly `die()` claiming no leg in the matrix satisfies astro's floor.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard each parsed segment with Number.isNaN before defaulting (e.g. `Number.isNaN(parts[1]) ? 0 : parts[1]`), or reject/fail loudly on a leg whose segments don't all parse as integers, consistent with the script's own "fail loud rather than silently misjudge" approach to the `>=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` floor format.

findings.description: The Check-4 `FIXTURE` (the TypeScript consumer that type-checks against the shipped `.d.ts` and then actually authorizes) imports from `@qadi/core`, `@qadi/promise`, `@qadi/testing`, `@qadi/react`, `@qadi/devtools` (both entry points), `@qadi/predicate-sql`, `@qadi/predicate-prisma`, and `@qadi/audit` — eight of the nine public packages. `@qadi/http` is packed, protocol-checked, exports-checked and runtime-import-probed in checks 0-3 like every other package, but it is never imported by the consumer fixture, so its shipped `.d.ts` is never type-checked against a real consumer and its behavior is never exercised end-to-end the way the doc comment says checks 3-4 are meant to ("@qadi/devtools ships TWO entry points... exercised here or nowhere" shows the FIXTURE is deliberately built to cover every package/entry point). A broken `.d.ts` or a regression in @qadi/http's published surface would pass this merge gate silently.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small @qadi/http import/usage to FIXTURE (e.g. build and mount its Effect-platform HTTP middleware against a test route) so all nine public packages are exercised by check 4, not eight.

findings.description: `no-static-layer-or-default`'s regex `/\bstatic\s+layer\b|\.Default\b/` bans any `.Default` member access unconditionally. That is correct for the `Effect.Service`-derived `.Default` static accessor the rule exists to forbid, but AGENTS.md §3 itself sanctions naming a plain standalone layer `Default` ("Default (the layer of a namespace-imported module)"). If such a layer were ever imported with a namespace import and accessed as `ModuleName.Default` (as opposed to being destructured), this rule would flag it as a violation even though it is the AGENTS.md-sanctioned pattern, not the banned one. No such usage exists in the codebase today (`grep -rn "\.Default\b" packages/*/src packages/*/test` returns nothing), so this is latent rather than live.
findings.suggestedFix: Narrow the second alternative to the actual pattern being banned (e.g. requiring the preceding identifier to look like a service/class reference such as `XxxService.Default`) or note in a comment that a namespace-imported `Default` layer should be destructured on import to avoid tripping this rule.
